transcript.text: Bit of a weird one - my son put the microwave on for 10 minutes with nothing in it by accident. Now there's a horrible smell. Is it broken?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. It may be damaged, yes. Do not use it again, even to test it with water: it needs a qualified microwave engineer to check it. The more likely possibilities are heat damage to the high-voltage cooking system, or scorching of residue/a small internal waveguide cover or cavity coating. The smell alone cannot safely distinguish them. 1. Open the door and look around the cavity, including the small flat panel on an inside wall or roof. Blackening, a hole, bubbling paint, melted plastic or scorch marks supports internal heat/arcing damage.
2. Remove the glass tray and look for any burnt food residue or melted material underneath. This may explain some smell, but it would not rule out damage from the empty run.
3. Do not remove the outer casing or any internal panels. Microwaves can retain dangerous high voltage even when unplugged. If there is any visible scorching or damage, leave it unplugged and arrange repair or replacement.

I had a look and there's a brownish mark on the panel on the side wall, and no old food or wrapper in there, it was empty. There was also a bit of smoke coming out of the side vents when I opened the door, and a hot electrical sort of smell. It's turned off at the switch but still plugged in. Is it safe or should I bin it?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If there are flames or smoke is still coming from it, keep away, don't open the door of an oven, microwave or dryer that is on fire, switch it off at the wall or the fuse box only if you can do that safely, get everyone out and call 999.

a horrible burnt smell is not normal afterwards

candidates: Overheated or damaged high-voltage cooking components after running empty (high)
Burnt food residue, waveguide cover or cavity coating (medium)

tags.checkGiven: With it unplugged and the door open, take out anything metal or foil, then look closely at the small flat cover panel on the inside wall (us

plan: They asked: "Is it broken?" - answer that first.

Safety: a burning hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
The fault they reported is: "horrible smell after running empty". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

hazards.clause: there was also a bit of smoke coming out of the side vents when i opened the door
